cachekey.env.windows.intro: This sets SMITH_CACHE_KEY for your user on this machine:
cachekey.env.windows.done: SMITH_CACHE_KEY is set for your user. New terminals pick it up. Terminals that are already open do not. To remove it, run: smith cache key --remove
cachekey.profile.intro: smith will add the key to {path}. These are the exact lines, with the key hidden:
cachekey.profile.warning: Warning: backups of your dotfiles and dotfile git repositories keep the key.
cachekey.profile.choices: Enter writes it   Esc cancels   h shows how to do it by hand
cachekey.profile.written: smith wrote the key to {path}. Open a new terminal to use it. Terminals that are already open do not have it. To remove it, run: smith cache key --remove
cachekey.profile.unsafe: The key has characters that a shell line cannot hold safely. Nothing was written.
cachekey.byhand.file: To do it by hand, add this line to {path}, with your key in place of <the key>:
cachekey.byhand.other: smith does not know a profile file for your shell. To do it by hand, add this line to the profile of your shell, with your key in place of <the key>:
cachekey.byhand.next: Then open a new terminal. smith changed nothing.
cachekey.remove.profile: Removed the smith cache key block from {path}
cachekey.remove.windows: SMITH_CACHE_KEY is no longer set for your user. Terminals that are already open keep it until they close.
cachekey.remove.none: smith found no cache key that it set. Nothing changed.
